issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The candidate uses only the training labels, makes no file or network calls, and takes all randomness from the seed through np.random.default_rng(seed).

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The change averages 15 Tanimoto-kernel SVRs, each trained on a random 60% of the fingerprint bits. The log1p/expm1 transform is the same as before and is applied the same way in both directions.

Minor risk: on a random bit subset, a molecule can have no set bits. tanimoto_kernel could then divide 0 by 0, unless it already guards against that, which the incumbent version may do. It does not seem to have happened here: the run scored normally and has no integrity flags.

The z score checks out: (0.5155 - 0.5175) / (0.0070 * sqrt(2)) = -0.20, matching the reported -0.203. The candidate is slightly worse and well within noise. Rejecting it is right: it adds code and about 15 times the kernel compute with no gain.
